preconditions.expression: all(1 <= n <= 200 and 1 <= m <= 200 and 1 <= k <= 200 for n, m, k in [int(x) for x in stdin.split()[:3]])
preconditions.description: Input dimensions n, m, k are integers within the bounds 1 ≤ n, m, k ≤ 200.

preconditions.expression: len([line for line in stdin.splitlines() if line.strip()]) == 1 + k + k
preconditions.description: Input consists of exactly 1 + k + k lines: one for n, m, k; k for starting positions; and k for target positions.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(sx) <= n and 1 <= int(sy) <= m for sx, sy in [line.split() for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:1+k]])
preconditions.description: Each starting position (sx_i, sy_i) is within the board bounds 1 ≤ sx_i ≤ n and 1 ≤ sy_i ≤ m.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(fx) <= n and 1 <= int(fy) <= m for fx, fy in [line.split() for line in stdin.splitlines()[1+k:1+2*k]])
preconditions.description: Each target position (fx_i, fy_i) is within the board bounds 1 ≤ fx_i ≤ n and 1 ≤ fy_i ≤ m.

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip() == '-1' or (len(stdout.splitlines()) == 2 and 0 < int(stdout.splitlines()[0]) <= 2 * n * m)
postconditions.description: Output is either -1 (impossible) or a sequence of 1 to 2nm operations, followed by the sequence of moves (L, R, U, D).

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip() == '-1' or all(any((sx_i + sum(1 if d == 'D' else -1 if d == 'U' else 0 for d in moves), sy_i + sum(1 if d == 'R' else -1 if d == 'L' else 0 for d in moves)) == (fx_i, fy_i) for i in range(k)) for (sx_i, sy_i), (fx_i, fy_i) in zip(start_positions, target_positions))
postconditions.description: For each chip, there exists at least one point in the move sequence where its position matches the target (fx_i, fy_i). The move sequence is derived from the second line of stdout, where moves is the sequence of characters (L, R, U, D).

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip() != '-1' and len(stdout.splitlines()[1]) == int(stdout.splitlines()[0]) and all(d in 'LRUD' for d in stdout.splitlines()[1])
postconditions.description: If a solution exists, the second line of stdout is exactly the number of operations specified in the first line, and consists only of valid move characters (L, R, U, D).
